# What this book is {.unnumbered}

This book is the guide to **ISLA** (Invariant Slice Attention), a neural
surrogate for steady, boundary-driven PDE problems. Given a discretized
boundary and the problem's global conditions, ISLA predicts the steady field
on that boundary and in the domain it bounds. The book is written the way a
user guide for a design code is written. It teaches what the method computes
and why each part is there. It shows how to run it. Then it lays out, with
the same care, what the measurements say for it and against it. The reader
we have in mind is fluent in PDE numerics and machine learning and has never
seen this program. Every term is defined where it first appears. Every
number is computed from a checked-in artifact as the page renders.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Where the name comes from"}
An *isla* is an island, a shape defined entirely by its boundary. The boundary is what the method takes as input.
The code class is `physicsnemo.experimental.models.ISLA`.
:::

## The thesis {#sec-verdict}

**ISLA is a slice-attention surrogate that is exactly equivariant to rigid
motions and consistent under a change of boundary discretization, and it
pays nothing in accuracy for either.** The two invariances are defined in
@sec-invariances. It is measured against GeoTransolver, the strongest
published slice-attention surrogate, and Transolver, with every model
given the same inputs and scored on the same instrument at the reporting
protocol of @sec-protocol. Each architecture runs at one reference configuration, the most
accurate of its architecture that trains under 80 GiB per GPU on the two
selection datasets, and every checkpoint is scored on the native validation
mesh and with every validation case rotated and translated; on the three
surface datasets whose meshes exceed the cell budget (the DrivAerML Surface
task, HiLiftAeroML and Shift-SUV) it is also scored on a uniform point cloud
of the surface. Rotated and translated, ISLA's error barely moves and the
baselines' error grows by factors, except on two structured solid meshes
where ISLA's own error moves too. On the uniform point cloud of those three
surface datasets, ISLA's error moves by at most 2% and the baselines' grows
by factors. On the DrivAerML Volume task the same draw changes only the
boundary sample, which only ISLA reads, and ISLA's interior error rises
several-fold through the queries' distance to the nearest boundary sample,
and on the AirfRANS interior task, with the airfoil thinned to 400
segments, a length-proportional draw about doubles ISLA's pressure and
velocity errors against a uniform draw of the same count; in distribution
the three are within seed noise on the cars, ISLA leads on the wings and
on interior velocity, and trails on tensor targets, on the lug under the
float32 protocol and on the sport-utility bodies. @tbl-thesis is the standing, one row per dataset and
task.

```{python}
#| label: setup-index
#| include: false
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
mean = statistics.mean

# Every standing row reads the dataset's three-protocol artifact (results/char/<dataset>.json): the three architectures at
# their reference configurations, scored on the native validation mesh, on a uniform point cloud at the same budget, and with
# every validation case rotated and translated. Arms are keyed by architecture (the arm label's first word).
def char_arms(artifact):
    C = json.load(open(RES / "char" / artifact))
    return C, {arm.split()[0]: d for arm, d in C["arms"].items()}
def fmt_ratio(r):
    """A ratio as the book writes it: two decimals near one, one decimal to ten, none above."""
    return f"{r:.0f}x" if r >= 10 else f"{r:.1f}x" if r >= 2 else f"{r:.2f}"
BASELINES = ("GeoTransolver", "Transolver")
ART = {name: char_arms(f) for name, f in (("surface", "drivaerml_surface.json"), ("hilift", "hilift_surface.json"),
                                          ("volume", "drivaerml_volume.json"), ("airfrans", "airfrans.json"),
                                          ("suv", "shift_suv_surface.json"), ("tensile2d", "tensile2d.json"), ("lug", "lug.json"),
                                          ("deepjeb", "deepjeb_surface.json"))}
rat = lambda name, arch, f, pk="native": ART[name][1][arch][pk][f]["mean"] / ART[name][1]["ISLA"][pk][f]["mean"]
shift = lambda name, arch, f, pk: ART[name][1][arch][pk][f]["mean"] / ART[name][1][arch]["native"][f]["mean"]
has = lambda name, arch: arch in ART[name][1]
pair = lambda name, f, pk="native": " / ".join(fmt_ratio(rat(name, a, f, pk)) if has(name, a) else "—" for a in BASELINES)
# which rows hold the final reference configurations is read from each artifact's ISLA arm label
FINAL = {name: "512 with 512 slices" in C["isla_arm"] for name, (C, _) in ART.items()}
label = lambda name: "final reference configurations" if FINAL[name] else "first-pass reference configurations"
NAMES = {"surface": "DrivAerML Surface", "hilift": "HiLiftAeroML", "volume": "DrivAerML Volume", "airfrans": "AirfRANS", "suv": "Shift-SUV", "tensile2d": "Tensile2d", "lug": "lug", "deepjeb": "DeepJEB++"}
lst = lambda flag: ", ".join(NAMES[n] for n in ART if FINAL[n] == flag)
three = lambda name, f, pks=("native", "area", "posed"): "; ".join(f"{lab} {pair(name, f, pk)}" for pk, lab in (("native", "native"), ("area", "point cloud"), ("posed", "posed")) if pk in pks)
tri = lambda name, fields, arch: " / ".join(f"{rat(name, arch, f):.2f}" for f in fields)
def word(name, arch, f):
    """One native baseline ÷ ISLA ratio in words: a lead or a deficit when every baseline seed sits on one side of every ISLA seed, level when the seeds interleave."""
    b = list(ART[name][1][arch]["native"][f]["per_seed"].values()); i = list(ART[name][1]["ISLA"]["native"][f]["per_seed"].values())
    if min(b) > max(i): return "leads"
    if max(b) < min(i): return "trails"
    return "is level"
# DeepJEB++: the ISLA lanes' trainer validation per epoch (the dataset chapter's trajectory artifact), for the epoch at which the
# half-rate lanes match the baselines and the epoch at which they fall to the mean-field plateau
JB_TRAJ = [J("char/deepjeb_trajectories_2026-10-07.json")["lanes"][r]["epochs"] for r in ("cl_jd_rate_e40_seed42", "cl_jd_rate_e40_seed43")]
jb_parity_epoch = max(int(min(e, key=lambda k: e[k]["val_loss"])) for e in JB_TRAJ)
def jb_collapse(e):
    """First validation epoch whose loss is more than twice the running minimum before it."""
    lo = float("inf")
    for k in sorted(e, key=int):
        if e[k]["val_loss"] > 2 * lo: return int(k)
        lo = min(lo, e[k]["val_loss"])
jb_collapse_epochs = [jb_collapse(e) for e in JB_TRAJ]
```

S, H, V, A, U, T, L = (ART[k][1] for k in ("surface", "hilift", "volume", "airfrans", "suv", "tensile2d", "lug"))

     tri("tensile2d", ("stress_l2", "displacement_l2", "q_l2"), "GeoTransolver") + "; " + tri("tensile2d", ("stress_l2", "displacement_l2", "q_l2"), "Transolver"),

for r in rows: out += "| " + " | ".join(r) + " |\n"

      "the DeepJEB++ row's ISLA lanes at half that rate; GeoTransolver width 256 at 200,000 cells; Transolver width 512 with 16 layers at 100,000 cells)"

         "at 100,000 cells, learning rate 2.5e-4; GeoTransolver and Transolver width 1,024 at 100,000 cells)" if lst(False) else "")
      + ". Every ISLA row was trained with the raw slice reads, before the normalized reads (@sec-arch-layer) became the "

## How to read this book {#sec-how-to-read}

**The book reads in order. Each chapter assumes only the ones before it.**

- **The problem and how we measure** (@sec-problem): the boundary-to-field
  operator and its general interface, taught on a two-dimensional airfoil
  whose exact solution we know, then the generalization axes, the metric
  and the instrument.
- **ISLA, one idea at a time** (@sec-isla): why each part of the
  architecture is there, from "a sum over cells should be an integral" to
  the equivariant output basis.
- **The two invariances ISLA is built for** (@sec-invariances): what
  rigid-motion equivariance and discretization consistency mean, what each
  buys, and every pose and discretization measurement of the book.
- **The ISLA forward pass** (@sec-architecture): the computation stage by
  stage, with every tensor shape and code identifier.
- **Baselines, datasets and the protocol** (@sec-baselines): GeoTransolver
  and Transolver, the dataset roster and the conventions they share, and
  the rules that make a comparison fair.
- **Using ISLA** (@sec-using): the reference configuration, the inputs, the
  commands, the sampler, checkpoints and cost.
- **Evidence, by dataset.** One chapter per dataset, each in the same
  order: the problem and its diversity, what is measured, the standing of
  the three architectures, the ladders and controls, and what the dataset
  does not say. DrivAerML, both tasks (@sec-drivaerml); HiLiftAeroML
  (@sec-hilift); AirfRANS (@sec-airfrans); Shift-SUV (@sec-shift-suv);
  PLAID Tensile2d (@sec-tensile2d); the GINOT bracket lug (@sec-lug);
  DeepJEB++ (@sec-deepjeb). Then capacity, scaling laws and cost
  (@sec-capacity), the one evidence chapter organized by question rather
  than by dataset.
- **Limits and open questions** (@sec-limits), then **program status**
  (@sec-program-status), the one chapter with dates.
- **Appendices.** The names and colors and the design-decision ledger
  (@sec-principled-decisions), ISLA against the literature
  (@sec-isla-vs-geotransolver), and the lab notebook (@sec-notebook): every
  preregistration, launch and verdict, including the failures, in the order
  they happened.

Every claim's scope is in @sec-limits, which also says what the book does
not claim.

Optional depth sits in collapsed notes like the one at the top of this
page. The throughline reads completely with all of them closed.
